name: Pressure on the nerve (compression)
description: The nerve is squeezed, for example by a disc, a narrowed canal or a tight tunnel. Pressure first blocks the larger fibres that carry touch, so it typically causes numbness and pins and needles, and with more pressure, weakness.

clues.reason: Pressure blocks the fibres that carry touch, so the skin they supply goes numb.
Squeezed fibres fire on their own, which is felt as pins and needles or buzzing.

These tests narrow the space around the nerve for a short time (the carpal tunnel, or the opening where a neck root leaves the spine).
A nerve irritated at a pressure point sends tingling along its path when tapped there.

name: Stretch on the nerve (tension)
description: Nerves have to slide and lengthen as the joints move. If a nerve is stuck or already irritated, putting the limb in a position that lengthens it hurts, often as a shooting or electric pain along its path.

clues.reason: A nerve sensitive to stretch hurts when the limb lengthens it. If stretching never brings it on, stretch is a less likely cause.
A sudden shooting, electric pain along a line is typical of a nerve being pulled.
These tests lengthen a nerve (the sciatic, femoral or ulnar). Reproducing your pain suggests that nerve is sensitive to stretch.

conditions.reason: An irritated L5 or S1 root is pulled when the straight leg is raised.

name: Rubbing on the nerve (friction)
description: A nerve that rubs over bone or a tight band with each movement is irritated by repetition rather than by one position.

clues.reason: Friction builds with repeated movement. If repetition doesn't affect it, rubbing is a less likely cause.
A nerve irritated by rubbing gives tingling in the area it supplies.

conditions.reason: In some people the ulnar nerve slips over the bony point of the inner elbow each time the elbow bends.

name: Reduced blood supply (ischaemia)
description: Nerves need a steady blood supply. When their blood vessels are squeezed, for example nerve roots in a narrowed spinal canal while walking, symptoms build with activity and settle within minutes of rest, like a limb that has 'gone to sleep'.

clues.reason: Symptoms from a nerve short of blood build with use and settle quickly with rest. If they don't, this is a less likely cause.
Leg symptoms on walking that ease by sitting or bending forward are the classic pattern of nerve roots short of blood in a narrowed canal.
A nerve short of blood fires abnormally: the same pins and needles as a foot that has gone to sleep.
The limb feels heavy and tired as the nerve runs short of blood.

conditions.reason: Walking upright narrows the canal further and is thought to cut the blood flow to the squeezed roots, which recovers on sitting or bending forward.
Night symptoms are thought to come partly from the nerve running short of blood while the wrist is bent during sleep.

Here it is the leg muscles, not a nerve, that run short of blood: narrowed arteries can't keep up with walking, and the pain settles with rest.
Pressure building inside the tight muscle compartment during exercise squeezes the small blood vessels, starving the muscle and nerves of blood until you stop.

name: Chemical irritation (inflammation)
description: Inflammatory chemicals, for example from disc material that has leaked onto a nerve root, make a nerve sensitive even without much pressure. The pain tends to be burning or deep, present at rest and at night, and worse with coughing or straining.

clues.reason: Chemical irritation doesn't switch off with rest. If the pain is never there at rest or at night, this is a less likely cause.
Burning is a common description of a chemically irritated nerve.

name: Immune attack on the nerve
description: Occasionally the body's immune system inflames a nerve directly, with nothing pressing on it. It typically starts suddenly with severe pain lasting days to weeks, followed by weakness as the pain settles.

clues.reason: This kind of attack almost always starts with sudden, severe pain. Without that, it is unlikely.
Weakness follows as the pain eases.

conditions.reason: An immune attack on the nerves of the shoulder and arm.

name: Damage from within (metabolic or toxic)
description: Some nerve damage comes from inside the body rather than from pressure: high blood sugar in diabetes, heavy alcohol use, a lack of vitamin B12, or some medicines such as chemotherapy. The longest nerves suffer first, so it usually starts in the toes of both feet and creeps upward, with numbness, tingling or burning.

clues.reason: Damage that starts with the longest nerves shows first in the toes or soles of both feet and spreads upward. If it started elsewhere or on one side, this is a less likely cause.
Both soles going numb together fits a cause that affects all the nerves evenly rather than one squeezed nerve.
Diabetes is a common cause of this kind of nerve damage.

conditions.reason: The nerves are damaged along their length by a body-wide cause, longest nerves first.

name: Direct injury (trauma or an operation)
description: A nerve can be bruised, stretched or cut by an injury, or damaged during an operation near it. Symptoms start at or soon after the event, in the area that nerve supplies.

clues.reason: An injured nerve gives symptoms from the time of the injury. Without one, this is unlikely.
Several nerves here are known to be injured during nearby operations.
A damaged nerve leaves the skin it supplies numb.

conditions.reason: The axillary nerve can be stretched when the shoulder dislocates.

name: Sensitised nervous system (sensitisation)
description: When pain goes on for a long time, the nerves and spinal cord can become more sensitive and turn up the volume of every signal. Light touch can then hurt, and the pain can spread beyond the original area. This can come on top of any long-lasting problem, so it isn't linked to one condition.

clues.reason: Pain from a light brush on the skin is thought to come from nerve cells in the spinal cord becoming more excitable, rather than from the injured nerve itself.
Pain that spreads well beyond the original area suggests the signals are being amplified.
Burning is common when the nervous system is sensitised.

name: Tissue overload: the nerve only carries the pain
description: Here the nerve itself is healthy. A tendon, joint, disc or muscle is overloaded or worn, and the nerves simply carry the pain signal from it. The pain tends to be dull, aching or tight, in an area you can point to, set off by using or pressing that structure, and without numbness.

clues.reason: Tissue pain comes from the structure itself, so pressing or loading it usually sets the pain off. In back pain from the spine's own tissues, the muscles are typically tender to pressure.
Pain from the spine's own tissues is typically dull and aching.
Overloaded or guarding muscles feel tight or cramp.
A sharp, catching pain with one movement often comes from a joint or tendon.
Tendons are overloaded by repeated movement.
A tendon, joint or muscle problem doesn't damage nerve fibres, so it rarely makes the skin numb. Among 1,083 people with back pain that didn't spread down the leg, 4.9% reported marked numbness.
Pins and needles is uncommon without a nerve problem. In the same group, 10.9% reported marked prickling.
Warmth relaxes tight or guarding muscle and eases stiff joints. It can ease nerve pain too, so it only fits, never rules out.
Joints and muscles stiffen when kept still and loosen once you get moving.

name: Inflamed joints or tendons (inflammatory disease)
description: Here the body's own inflammation, from an immune disease, crystals or an infection, attacks the lining of joints, tendon attachments or the spine. Unlike wear or overload, the pain is often worst after rest, with long morning stiffness, swelling, warmth or redness, and it can affect several places at once.

clues.reason: Inflammation builds up overnight, so the stiffness after waking lasts well over half an hour.
Inflamed joints swell, and crystal attacks make them red and hot.
Inflammation hurts at rest too, unlike pain from overload.
